column1: Geometry Gains — per-satellite gain, actual errors, stealth window and dropped reports (manuscript supplementary material, v2.0)

Assumed Walker-Star variants, 200 satellites, 500 km, inclination 86 deg, aircraft at 10 km; 12,960 samples per variant (19 latitudes x 8 longitudes x 90 epochs). e_h = g_i*eps; HDOP^2 = sum g_i^2; h* = 350/30 = 11.7 is a necessary-condition screening threshold. Sections B and C use the RAIM-style residual monitor of geometry/raim.py (chi-square test with n-3 degrees of freedom, P_FA = P_MD = 1e-3, minimum detectable bias sigma*sqrt(lambda/(1-h_ii)), protection level g_i*eps_det,i); the monitor of the reference design is not published, so this is an assumption, and sigma = 10, 30, 100 m is illustrative. The 350 m statistic (RMS, percentile, maximum) is to be confirmed against the standard. Scripts: geometry/hdop*.py, gain*.py, raim.py; seeds 1 and 7.

B. Stealth window under the assumed RAIM-style residual monitor (geometry/raim.py; P_FA = P_MD = 1e-3; eps_L1 = 29.98 m). Omega_L3: share of samples with an open L3 window; Omega: share in which the clock route is also open (equal for all sigma). k = factor by which the threshold is raised; k = 2, 4 model the enabler T3.06.
C. Reports dropped (T2.04): variant A 10x20, 0 deg; best of 400 subsets per sample (a lower bound); m reports kept. g_max: gain of the best-placed satellite, median of the best subset.

column2: Gain of the best-placed satellite is about half the HDOP in the median sample (ratio 0.47-0.55); in the tail the two coincide. A 30 m step breaches 350 m only where g_max >= 11.7. With the residual monitor, the clock route (Omega) is closed in the nominal variant A at every sigma and opens in 0.3 to 11 % of the samples of the sparser variants; after T2.04 it is open in at least 3.7, 32 and 54 % of the samples with 6, 4 and 3 reports left. Omega_L3 alone is open in 0.6, 8 and 60 % of the nominal samples of variant A for sigma = 10, 30, 100 m. Monte-Carlo check of the linear model: simulated rms error agrees with sigma*HDOP within 2.3 % (geometry/gain2.py). The results are those of geometry/raim_results.json, which the paper reports in its stealth-window table.
